title: Share trading policy - Policy on directors and employees dealing in securities

tiers.name: directors
tiers.description: Directors of Lynas Corporation Limited. Same substantive prohibitions as employees; distinguished only in that clearance is sought from the Chairman (who makes enquiries of other directors) rather than the Secretary, and in the ASX and company secretary notification obligations in sections 10 and 11.

tiers.name: employees
tiers.description: All employees of the Company. Same substantive prohibitions as directors; clearance is sought from the Secretary. No sub-tier of executives, KMP or 'restricted persons' is created.

windows.start_anchor: 1 Business Day after the release of annual, half yearly or quarterly results
windows.end_anchor: three weeks after the release of annual, half yearly or quarterly results

windows.start_anchor: 1 Business Day after the Annual General Meeting of the Company's shareholders
windows.end_anchor: three weeks after the Annual General Meeting

windows.start_anchor: 1 Business Day after the Company issues a prospectus
windows.end_anchor: three weeks after the Company issues a prospectus

windows.start_anchor: expiry of an open period under paragraph 7.1 (three weeks after results, AGM or prospectus)
windows.end_anchor: commencement of the next open period under paragraph 7.1, or clearance under paragraph 9.2

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No separate ad hoc blackout power is conferred. The Chairman and Secretary retain a residual discretion to withhold clearance within an open period where undisclosed price sensitive information exists: they 'will generally allow' dealing 'unless there is in existence price sensitive information that has not been disclosed because of an ASX Listing Rule exception' (7.1), and no dealing may proceed until the Chairman or Secretary 'has indicated in writing that there is no impediment' (6.1(4)). The policy does not say whether a refusal or the reason for it is confidential.

rules.detail: Section 14 is an express derivatives rule but it bites only in prohibited periods: trading in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities is prohibited during prohibited periods, which under 7.3 means all time outside the three-week open windows. Outside those prohibited periods a derivative is permitted, subject to the general 6.1 gateway (no price sensitive information, advise the Chairman or Secretary, written confirmation of no impediment). No venue limitation is drawn, so an OTC put and call written by a bank is covered on the same footing as an exchange-traded option.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees are prohibited from trading during prohibited periods in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: During a prohibited period (all time other than the three-week windows in 7.1 and a 9.2 exceptional-circumstances clearance) an OTC collar cannot be entered, amended, rolled or settled. Section 9.2 relief is confined to a sale of securities and does not extend to derivative trading.
rules.evidence: All periods other than the periods referred to in paragraphs 7.1 and 9.2 are “closed periods” during which all directors and employees are generally prohibited from Dealing in Securities of the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute, at all times ban, but narrowly drawn: it catches only the hedging of options issued under an employee option plan before those options vest. It does not by its terms extend to unvested performance rights or unvested shares, nor to options after vesting.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees must not at any time hedge options issued to them under an employee option plan prior to vesting of the options.

rules.detail: Hedging vested holdings is not named. The 13.2 ban stops at vesting, so by negative implication hedging vested options and shares is not prohibited; it is instead controlled as trading in a financial product over the Company's securities (14.1, barred in prohibited periods) and by the 6.1 clearance gateway. The policy does not define hedging or 'limiting economic risk' and draws no vested-but-locked category.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees must not at any time hedge options issued to them under an employee option plan prior to vesting of the options.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. A prepaid forward or collar is an agreement in relation to shares in the Company and so a Deal In Securities, and is also a financial product created over the Company's securities under 14.1. It therefore needs the 6.1 written no-impediment confirmation and must be entered inside a 7.1 open window.
rules.evidence: Deal In Securities means apply for, buy or sell shares, options or other securities in the Company, or enter into agreements in relation to shares, options or other securities in the Company and includes procuring another person to do any of these things

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere named and is not listed in the definition of Deal In Securities. A short sale would still be a 'sell' of securities in the Company and so a Dealing subject to 6.1 and the closed-period regime, and closing a short position would in practice engage the at all times short-term trading ban in 13.1, but neither is stated.
Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned anywhere and are not swept into the definition of Deal In Securities.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Lynas shares is a financial product created over or in respect of the Company's securities and so is barred during prohibited periods by 14.1 and needs 6.1 clearance in an open window; in practice a CFD would also be characterised as short-term trading, which 13.1 bans at all times.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not named and is not prohibited. The policy positively contemplates that directors and employees may have securities pledged to a secured lender, because it carves a lender's enforcement sale out of the policy altogether. There is no disclosure obligation, price trigger guidance, cap on the proportion of the holding that may be pledged, or requirement to notify the company of a facility.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights;

rules.detail: Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Lynas securities is not named and is not within the definition of Deal In Securities, which reaches applications, purchases, sales and agreements in relation to securities. Charging shares to a bank as collateral is therefore not itself a Dealing needing clearance, and the exclusion of secured lender enforcement sales confirms that encumbrances are contemplated.
rules.evidence: a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights;

rules.detail: There is no prohibition on secured financing of any kind, whether a margin loan or a bespoke facility secured on Lynas shares, and no approval, notification or scope limit. The only provision on the subject is the excluded trading item protecting the borrower from breach when the lender enforces.
rules.evidence: The following transactions relating to trading in the Company's securities are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights;

rules.detail: Blanket, at all times ban on short-term trading in the Company's securities, with no defined holding period, no LIFO or intention test and no carve-out for plan securities. The absence of a definition leaves the boundary to the Chairman and Secretary at the 6.1 clearance stage.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.

clearance.approver: Chairman, after making appropriate enquiries of other directors
clearance.post_trade_to: company secretary; and ASX (Appendix 3Y, the Company acting as the director's agent under section 205G)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately on acquiring or disposing of a relevant interest (company secretary); ASX notification within 5 Business Days by the Company and within 14 days under section 205G
clearance.evidence: they have advised the Chairman (in the case of directors) ... of their intention to do so; ... the Chairman or Secretary has indicated in writing that there is no impediment to them doing so. ... Directors must notify the company secretary immediately on acquiring or disposing of a relevant interest in any securities in the Company.

clearance.approver: Secretary, after making appropriate enquiries of other directors
clearance.evidence: they have advised ... the Secretary (in the case of employees) of their intention to do so; the Chairman or Secretary (as the case may be) has made appropriate enquiries of other directors; the Chairman or Secretary has indicated in writing that there is no impediment to them doing so

short_term.evidence: Directors and employees must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.

exceptions.evidence: transfers which result in no change in the beneficial interest in the securities;

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the Company's securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;

where a director or employee is a trustee, trading in the Company's securities by that trust provided the director or employee is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the director or employee;
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer;

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board;
a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights;
the exercise (but not sale of securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security;

exceptions.approver: prior clearance in accordance with procedures set out in the trading policy
exceptions.evidence: trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior clearance has been provided ... the director or employee may not cancel the trading plan or cancel or otherwise vary the terms of his or her participation in the trading plan during a prohibited period other than in exceptional circumstances.

exceptions.approver: Chairman and at least one other non-executive director
exceptions.evidence: In exceptional circumstances, where it is the only reasonable course of action available to a director or employee, clearance may be given by the Chairman and at least one other non-executive director for the director or employee to sell (but not to purchase) securities when he or she otherwise would not be permitted to do so by this policy.

external_documents: The Lynas Way (code of conduct, policies, structures and systems, work practices), referred to at 1.3-1.4 but not reproduced
The 'procedures set out in the trading policy' for prior clearance of a non-discretionary trading plan, referred to at 8.1(8) but not in fact set out in this document
exemption_authority: The board may grant a specific exemption from the policy: directors and employees 'should consider this policy to be binding on them in the absence of specific exemption by the board' (2.2). Separately, the Chairman and at least one other non-executive director may clear a sale, but not a purchase, in exceptional circumstances where it is the only reasonable course of action available (9.2), and only if the person is not in possession of undisclosed price sensitive information (9.5).

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following transactions relating to trading in the Company's securities are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising its rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the single most collar-friendly clause in the policy: the bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares, including a sale in a closed period, falls outside the policy altogether, so the executive does not breach by reason of the lender enforcing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no margin lending, secured financing, pledge or encumbrance prohibition of any kind, and no disclosure obligation in respect of any such facility.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is unrestricted, which is unusual among ASX policies and removes the usual blocking provision.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees are prohibited from trading during prohibited periods in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs are financial products over Lynas securities, so entry, amendment, roll, unwind and any cash or physical settlement of the collar must all be timed to fall inside a three-week open window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All periods other than the periods referred to in paragraphs 7.1 and 9.2 are “closed periods” during which all directors and employees are generally prohibited from Dealing in Securities of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lynas is closed by default and open only for three weeks after results, the AGM or a prospectus, so there may be as little as four short windows a year in which a collar can be struck or unwound.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance may be given by the Chairman and at least one other non-executive director for the director or employee to sell (but not to purchase) securities when he or she otherwise would not be permitted to do so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Out-of-window relief is confined to selling, so it cannot be used to buy back a written call, close out a put or enter a collar outside a window; only an outright sale of the underlying can be cleared.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested options
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees must not at any time hedge options issued to them under an employee option plan prior to vesting of the options.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging prohibition is confined to unvested employee options, so a collar over vested shares is not caught by it, but unvested option entitlements must be excluded from the collared parcel.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees must not at any time engage in short-term trading in securities of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: With no defined holding period, a short-dated collar or one with early termination or roll features risks being characterised as short-term trading, so a long tenor and confirmation from the Chairman or Secretary at clearance are advisable.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Chairman or Secretary has indicated in writing that there is no impediment to them doing so; and the proposed Dealing is permitted under paragraph 7.1 or 9.2.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy sets no window within which a cleared trade must be executed and no express revocation right, so the bank should document that the written no-impediment confirmation is current at pricing and at each subsequent leg.

bespoke_clauses.clause: directors and employees should consider this policy to be binding on them in the absence of specific exemption by the board.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The board can exempt a specific transaction from the policy entirely, which offers a route to sanction a collar whose timing or structure does not fit the narrow windows.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy has been implemented to prevent the incidence of 'insider trading' ... by directors and employees and persons associated with any of them. ... a director or employee must not recommend or otherwise suggest to any person (including a spouse, relative, friend, trustee of a family trust or directors of a family company) that they buy or sell securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Associates are referred to in the introduction but no associate is defined and no operative rule binds them, so a collar entered by a spouse or family trust sits in an untested area rather than a clearly permitted or prohibited one.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors must notify the company secretary immediately on acquiring or disposing of a relevant interest in any securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering the collar may change the director's relevant interest, or be treated as doing so on physical settlement, triggering immediate notice to the company secretary and an Appendix 3Y within 5 Business Days that will disclose the structure publicly.

summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable under this policy, which is markedly more permissive than most ASX policies on the financing leg. There is no prohibition on margin lending, secured financing, pledging or encumbering Lynas securities, granting security is not within the definition of Deal In Securities, and paragraph 8.1(6) expressly excludes from the policy a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights, so the bank's enforcement sale would not put the executive in breach even in a closed period. The derivative legs are the constraint: a put and call over Lynas shares are financial products created over the Company's securities and cannot be traded during prohibited periods (14.1), and since 7.3 makes every period a closed period except the three weeks following results, the AGM or a prospectus, entry, roll, unwind and settlement must each be timed into one of those narrow windows and preceded by written confirmation of no impediment from the Chairman (directors) or Secretary (employees). The 13.2 hedging ban reaches only employee options before vesting, so vested shares may be collared, but the undefined at all times ban on short-term trading in 13.1 argues for a long tenor and for clearing the structure explicitly. Out-of-window relief under 9.2 covers only a sale of securities, not derivative dealings, so no exceptional-circumstances route exists for an emergency unwind, and directors should expect the position to surface through immediate notification to the company secretary and an Appendix 3Y.
